cards.title: Mine 1- and 5-Star Reviews for the Failed-Solution Buyer
cards.summary: Identify buyers who already spent money on solutions that did not work — the source's definition of a best prospect.
cards.use_when: You are hunting for high-intent, self-aware prospects and want pain-point language they will recognize instantly.

cards.title: Reddit for Emotional Mechanics, Quora for Tactics
cards.summary: Split forum research by platform: use Reddit for raw feelings and barriers, avoid Quora when you need emotional pain points.
cards.use_when: You are choosing where to dig for psychological hurdles rather than tactical how-to answers.

cards.title: Track Repeated Words and Counterintuitive Benefit Connections
cards.summary: Use word frequency and surprising link patterns in forum threads to surface emotional benefits beyond the obvious outcome.
cards.use_when: You have a pile of forum answers and need to convert them into avatar language and benefit angles.

cards.title: Run Primary Customer Interviews With a Lateral Question Approach
cards.summary: Go beyond online reading by talking to real people, using indirect questions that surface context rather than pitching your idea.
cards.use_when: You have desk research and want to validate and deepen it with real conversations before building.

cards.title: Keep Qualitative Research Manual and Quote-Based
cards.summary: Deliberate ban on automating review and forum parsing so you absorb emotional nuance and exact vocabulary.
cards.use_when: You are mining reviews or forum threads and feel tempted to script, scrape, or summarize with an algorithm.

cards.title: Don't Chase Every Piece of Feedback
cards.summary: Reconcile contradictory reviews before changing your product or positioning.
cards.use_when: You are reading critical reviews and trying to decide which complaints to act on.

cards.title: Use Economic Signals to Gauge Whether a Market Supports Your Idea
cards.summary: Study whether competitors look like serious, profitable businesses before committing to a niche.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether a niche has commercial backing for a paid product or offer.

cards.title: Avatar vs. Demographic: The Empty-Nester Test
cards.summary: Why 'women 45+' is a demographic, not an avatar, and the specific-context standard that separates them.
cards.use_when: You are about to write ad copy, a VSL or a landing page and want to check whether you actually know who you are writing to.

cards.title: 60-Minute Manual Research Sprint: 80/20 Reddit and Amazon
cards.summary: The source's one-hour protocol: 30 minutes on public forums and 30 minutes on Amazon reviews, manually copying verbatim text.
cards.use_when: You have picked a demographic and need to build a real avatar without defaulting to AI-generated personas.

cards.title: Search Query Craft for Avatar Research
cards.summary: How to write search queries as the avatar to surface the rawest forum threads on their problem.
cards.use_when: You are starting the forum half of a manual research sprint and need to find threads worth mining.

cards.title: Copy Verbatim and Bold: Building the Language Library
cards.summary: The mechanical habit of pasting raw quotes into a doc and marking emotional language, failed solutions and situational context.
cards.use_when: You are in a research session and need a repeatable way to capture material you can actually write from.

cards.title: Emotional Mind States: Frustration vs. Fear
cards.summary: Identify the dominant emotion behind the problem because each mind state needs different copy.
cards.use_when: You have raw research and need to decide the emotional register your ads should use.

cards.title: Mine Named Failed Solutions, Not Generic Categories
cards.summary: Extract the exact products and procedures the avatar already tried so copy can name them specifically.
cards.use_when: You are writing hooks or objection-handling copy and want to reference failed prior attempts credibly.

cards.title: Understanding Before Curiosity: How to Build a Hook
cards.summary: Curiosity-driven hooks fail alone; pair deep understanding of the avatar's situation with attention-grabbing phrasing.
cards.use_when: You are writing hook lines and want to avoid clever-but-empty angles that make the avatar roll their eyes.

cards.title: Use AI as a Supplement, Not a Substitute for Research
cards.summary: The source's argument for manual research first: AI is efficient but becomes a crutch when you do not know what you are looking for.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to run deep-research prompts instead of doing forum and review mining yourself.

cards.title: Avatar Record Requirements: Quotes, Trigger, Job
cards.summary: The minimum contents any avatar must have in your library before it is usable for creative work.
cards.use_when: You are cataloguing research into avatar records or auditing whether an existing avatar is complete.

cards.title: Research Before Scaling: The $10k-Day Premise and Its Limits
cards.summary: The source's argument that avatar clarity gates scaling, framed with its commercial context and limitations.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how much research effort to invest before spending on ads or scaling a proven offer.

cards.title: Pre-Existing Insecurity Changes How You Write
cards.summary: Segment avatars by whether the problem stacks on top of existing confidence issues, because the copy register differs.
cards.use_when: You are drafting copy for a problem where some buyers are already confident and others are not.

cards.title: Replace Demographic Profiles With Situational Avatars
cards.summary: Why broad demographic targeting fails and how to build avatars around trigger moments, failed solutions, and identity loss instead.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why creatives or offers aren't differentiating, or when starting avatar research from scratch.

cards.title: Mine Competitor 1-Star Reviews for Failure and Trust Markers
cards.summary: Extracting explicit mechanical flaws, trust breaks, and repeated claims from 1-star competitor reviews to feed ad hooks and objections.
cards.use_when: Sourcing granular complaints, objections, and physical product friction before writing creatives or landing pages.

cards.title: Run Direct Phone Calls and Post-Purchase Surveys at Scale
cards.summary: The source's core sourcing routine: continuous outbound contact with existing buyers plus an automated Shopify survey to surface unvarnished lifestyle limitations.
cards.use_when: When you have buyers and need primary evidence of day-to-day friction, concerns, and language you can't get from reviews alone.

cards.title: Mine Condition-Specific Reddit Forums and Niche Groups
cards.summary: Using community forums as a source of clinical vocabulary, condition-specific pain points, and untapped angles.
cards.use_when: Researching a health, hobby, or subculture niche where customers congregate and describe their situation in their own terms.

cards.title: Match Phrasing to the Age Cohort and Platform
cards.summary: Same condition, different cohort, different words: catalog exact vernacular differences so ads sound like the customer, not the marketer.
cards.use_when: Writing ad copy and choosing channels for a specific cohort you're targeting.

cards.title: Build Belief Through the Avatar's Sequence of Failed Attempts
cards.summary: Structuring creative and landing-page narratives from the buyer's own journey: problem, past failure, why it failed, then the new mechanism.
cards.use_when: Writing ads or landing pages for a researched avatar and converting objections into hooks.

cards.title: Let Avatar Research Make the Offer Feel Bespoke
cards.summary: Reframing: the offer is not just the bundle and price but the expectations and language set through deep avatar understanding.
cards.use_when: Positioning a commodity product against identical competitors, or when testing offers and framing.

cards.title: Set the Universal Avatar Baseline: Quotes, Trigger, Job
cards.summary: A minimum evidence standard for every avatar record so personas don't drift back into demographic fields with no job.
cards.use_when: Creating or auditing avatar documents, and onboarding writers or media buyers to them.

cards.title: 5W Avatar Framework for Ecommerce Market Research
cards.summary: A five-question framework (Who, What, When, Where, Why) for defining an ecommerce customer avatar before writing marketing copy or building offers.
cards.use_when: Starting a new business, launching a new offer, or entering a new niche and you need a structured avatar before producing marketing assets.

cards.title: Avoid Focus Groups and Leading Surveys for Market Research
cards.summary: Traditional market research methods such as focus groups, badly worded surveys, and academic white papers are flagged as expensive, biased or outdated compared with direct intent mining.
cards.use_when: Choosing which research method to invest time and budget in, or deciding whether a proposed focus group or survey is worth running.

cards.title: Google Autocomplete to Map Search Intent
cards.summary: Use Google's autocomplete suggestions to enumerate long-tail search intent around a core niche keyword before sizing volume.
cards.use_when: Early niche or offer research when you need to discover the language and sub-topics your market actually searches for.

cards.title: Size Niche Keywords and Spot Seasonality in Keyword Planner
cards.summary: Use Google Ads Keyword Planner's 'discover new keywords' flow to pull keyword ideas with volume, competition and trend data for a target geography.
cards.use_when: After autocomplete mining, when you need to size demand, compare sub-topics, or check whether a niche has seasonal patterns.

cards.title: Amazon Autocomplete and Book Titles for Purchase Intent
cards.summary: Amazon surfaces what people actually buy via autocomplete, optimized book titles/subtitles, and listing copy that reflects real market language.
cards.use_when: Validating that a niche has real buyers and harvesting market-tested language, after search-intent research on Google.

cards.title: Amazon Review Mining and Review-Count Sales Estimation
cards.summary: Read Amazon reviews to extract what buyers liked and disliked, and use review counts as a rough proxy for sales velocity.
cards.use_when: Estimating demand and gathering voice-of-customer language for a specific product or niche on Amazon.

cards.title: Facebook Ad Library to Identify Profitable Competitor Angles
cards.summary: Use Meta's Ad Library via a competitor's Page Transparency to find which ad angles have run longest, as duration is treated as a proxy for profitability.
cards.use_when: Researching competitor messaging and offer angles in industries with active Meta advertising, after you have defined your avatar.

cards.title: Separate What Customers Say From What They Buy
cards.summary: Stated wants (search behaviour) and actual purchases (retail behaviour) are two different datasets and both are required for useful market research.
cards.use_when: Designing a research plan or deciding how much weight to give survey-style stated preferences versus behavioural evidence.

cards.title: Miracles and Miseries Extraction for Marketing Angles
cards.summary: Convert avatar research into two concrete lists — desired outcomes and pains — and turn them into marketing angles.
cards.use_when: Moving from raw avatar research into copy themes, ad angles and offer framing.

cards.title: Research Top 20% of Existing Customers for a New Offer
cards.summary: When launching a new offer to an existing audience, base the avatar on your top 20% of customers rather than on imagined demographics.
cards.use_when: You already have a customer base and are preparing a new offer, upsell or product line for that same market.

cards.title: Social Media Demographics Search for Platform Placement
cards.summary: A quick search for platform demographic data tells you which groups use which social channels, informing where to place content.
cards.use_when: Deciding which platforms to prioritise for content and campaigns based on your avatar's actual presence.

cards.title: Life Events and Daily Schedules as Buying Triggers
cards.summary: The 'When' lens targets moments in the customer's life and day that change buying behaviour and content consumption.
cards.use_when: Planning campaign timing, seasonal pushes, or content scheduling around your avatar's routines and transitions.

cards.title: Demographic, Geographic and Psychographic Layering for Ecommerce Avatars
cards.summary: Build the 'Who' layer as three stacked dimensions — demographics, geographics and psychographics — rather than demographics alone.
cards.use_when: Constructing an avatar document that will be handed to copywriters, media buyers or creative teams.

cards.title: Boundary Between Research, Creative, Media and Web Work
cards.summary: Market research and avatar work sits upstream of ad production, media buying and landing-page implementation and should hand off cleanly.
cards.use_when: Scoping who does what when planning a launch so research outputs are not confused with execution deliverables.

cards.title: Judge Whether an Ad's Longevity Signals Profitability
cards.summary: Ad duration is a usable but imperfect proxy for profitability; apply informed judgment and corroborate before treating a long-running ad as proven.
cards.use_when: Screening competitor ads in the Meta Ad Library and deciding which angles to model or test.

cards.title: Why Deeper Motivation Belongs in the Avatar
cards.summary: The 'Why' step converts features and benefits into motivation, telling you which benefits to lead with.
cards.use_when: Writing the value proposition or offer copy after the Who, What, When and Where steps are complete.

cards.title: Differentiate a saturated product with a new avatar instead of a new mechanism
cards.summary: When your product has no genuine mechanical or visual differentiation, compete by finding an unserved buyer group rather than fighting incumbents head-on.
cards.use_when: You are sourcing or marketing a saturated dropshipping product (e.g., an AB stimulator) and deciding how to enter a market dominated by 7-figure brands.

cards.title: Use Facebook Ad Library to map and exclude the mainstream avatar
cards.summary: Scan competitor creatives in the Ad Library to build a psychographic profile of the avatar you must avoid competing against.
cards.use_when: You need to know which demographics and desires incumbents already own before choosing an untapped avatar.

cards.title: Mine Amazon reviews for outlier buyer stories
cards.summary: Long Amazon reviews that narrate a buyer's life reveal alternative avatars distinct from the mainstream target.
cards.use_when: After mapping the incumbent avatar, you want candidate buyer segments your product already serves but competitors ignore.

cards.title: Validate avatar market size and problem severity on Reddit
cards.summary: Search Reddit threads to confirm a candidate avatar is a real, recurring, emotionally acute problem with enough people to scale against.
cards.use_when: You have a candidate avatar from review mining and need evidence it is large and painful enough to justify a campaign.

cards.title: Assemble a raw avatar profile before deep research
cards.summary: Compile the observational evidence from ads and reviews into a bare-bones avatar sketch that deep research can later expand.
cards.use_when: You are between discovery and deep research and need a structured starting input for an AI prompt or manual research.

cards.title: Run an AI deep-research prompt to produce a full avatar report
cards.summary: Feed a preliminary avatar sketch to ChatGPT or Gemini in deep-research mode to synthesise psychology, beliefs and verbatim language from public sources into a long report.
cards.use_when: You have prioritised one avatar and need comprehensive psychological and situational detail before writing copy.

cards.title: Prioritise avatars with zero paid competition over better-known segments
cards.summary: Choose the avatar that appears completely isolated from existing advertising, provided the burden of proof on size and pain is met.
cards.use_when: You have two or three candidate avatars and must pick one to build a campaign around.

cards.title: Turn the avatar record into copy-ready psychological inputs
cards.summary: A complete avatar record should contain the specific categories of insight that feed long-form ad copy and creative.
cards.use_when: You are finalising research to hand off to copywriting or creative development (the source routes writing to a separate copy module).

cards.title: Match the differentiation route to the product's actual state
cards.summary: If you have a genuinely different product, compete on a new mechanism; if it is the same commodity item, compete on a new avatar.
cards.use_when: Deciding strategy at the start of marketing a product in a saturated or dropshipped category.

cards.title: Three-tier audience taxonomy: TAM, ICP and persona
cards.summary: Separate total addressable market, fit-based ICP and buying-committee personas to plan reach, campaigns and metric vocabulary.
cards.use_when: You or a colleague keep conflating TAM, ICP and persona, or campaign briefs lack a clear audience boundary before content planning.

cards.title: Run five 30-minute qualitative customer interviews
cards.summary: A quick, low-cost interview protocol: pick your top five customers and ask for 30 minutes each to capture language and situation.
cards.use_when: You lack a documented ICP or persona and need raw customer language fast, or want the qualitative layer that surveys and CRM fields cannot provide.

cards.title: Source data externally and pull CRM firmographics
cards.summary: Combine external research (surveys, interviews, social mining) with internal CRM fields to assemble the ICP data picture.
cards.use_when: You are assembling ICP data and trying to work out where the evidence should come from for a specific company size.

cards.title: Synthesize unstructured transcripts into an ICP with an LLM
cards.summary: Feed call transcripts, survey data, CRM firmographics and content performance into an LLM and ask it to define the ICP and surface themes.
cards.use_when: You have raw qualitative data and need to turn it into a tangible ICP or persona document for the team and tools.

cards.title: Use a live LLM persona as an on-demand focus group
cards.summary: Keep the ICP or persona in an interactive LLM project so marketers can test whether copy, campaigns and positioning will resonate before publishing.
cards.use_when: Your persona lives in a PDF nobody opens, or marketers need a fast way to stress-test messaging, positioning and content ideas.

cards.title: Set content altitude by persona seniority
cards.summary: Use the persona to decide whether a topic is covered at the introductory 101 level or the advanced 301 level.
cards.use_when: You are planning content topics and there is disagreement about how deep or advanced the coverage should be.

cards.title: Separate ICP data layer from persona scope: firmographics vs committee roles
cards.summary: Keep firmographic target-account data at the ICP level and role-specific tasks, goals and metric vocabulary at the persona level.
cards.use_when: You are building the ICP record and need to decide which fields belong to the account profile versus each buying-committee member.

cards.title: Use social communities when CRM and transcripts are missing
cards.summary: Mine Reddit, LinkedIn and Instagram pain-point threads when you have no CRM data or call transcripts to start from.
cards.use_when: You are starting from zero data and cannot yet run customer interviews or pull CRM records.

cards.title: Avatar discovery via review mining
cards.summary: Mine competitor, marketplace and own-product reviews for identity phrases to uncover hidden buyer segments.
cards.use_when: You are picking a product to sell or launching a brand and need to identify which distinct buyer groups already buy something like it.

cards.title: Survey existing buyers to name your avatar
cards.summary: Use a free form and email to ask customers how they describe themselves, their situation and how the product helps.
cards.use_when: You have an existing customer list and want to turn implicit buyer segments into explicitly named avatars.

cards.title: Talk to customers directly to detect your dominant avatar
cards.summary: One-on-one and group conversations reveal which avatar actually dominates your customer base.
cards.use_when: You already sell to a mixed audience and want to know which single avatar deserves concentrated messaging.

cards.title: Market sophistication forces broad markets to fracture into sub-avatars
cards.summary: As buyers try and fail with generic offers, they demand specialists, creating niche avatar opportunities.
cards.use_when: You are choosing whether to address a whole market or a specialist slice of it, and need a reason to niche down.

cards.title: Test whether a niche is big enough before specialising
cards.summary: Sub-niches can be too small to sustain a business, so check the size of the parent market before niching down.
cards.use_when: You have identified a sub-avatar and must decide whether to build a brand or offer exclusively for it.

cards.title: Map sub-avatars through social content
cards.summary: Watch how general niches split into distinct subcultures on TikTok and similar platforms.
cards.use_when: You want to find or anticipate emergent buyer subcultures inside a category you already understand.

cards.title: Define an avatar by growth signals, not a definition
cards.summary: Treat an avatar as a group that is measurably growing in your reviews, customer base or community.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether an observed segment is a real avatar worth building around or just noise.

cards.title: Enter emerging trends as the first dedicated brand
cards.summary: When a new pastime takes off, sell into it as the first brand dedicated to participants rather than competing on the core equipment.
cards.use_when: You spot a fast-growing recreational trend and want a lower-competition entry point than the obvious product category.

cards.title: How deep niching fits ecommerce and dropshipping
cards.summary: The same avatar structure translates from agency niches to ecom brands by pointing a mass-market play at one sub-avatar.
cards.use_when: You are an ecommerce or dropshipping operator considering whether avatar specialisation applies to your model.

cards.title: Tailor the whole funnel to one avatar, not just the hook
cards.summary: Avatar fit must run through creative, primary text, page, proof and sales conversation — putting the avatar only in the hook is the common mistake.
cards.use_when: You have chosen an avatar and are rebuilding ads and landing/product pages to match it.

cards.title: Keep broad targeting while narrowing the avatar
cards.summary: Pair avatar-specific creative with broad targeting and let Facebook's algorithm locate the matching audience.
cards.use_when: You are running Meta ads for a niche avatar and deciding whether to narrow the audience settings.

cards.title: Rebrand existing products for a single avatar
cards.summary: Take products that already exist in other niches and market them exclusively to one avatar.
cards.use_when: You want to serve a newly forming avatar without developing new products from scratch.

cards.title: Four-pronged buyer research methodology
cards.summary: Combine qualitative customer conversations, quantitative surveys, digital intelligence tools and social listening to answer who your buyers are, how they behave and why.
cards.use_when: You need to build or rebuild buyer personas and want evidence-based insights rather than assumptions or template personas.

cards.title: Run 30-minute discovery calls, not sales calls
cards.summary: Frame customer interviews explicitly as exploratory conversations about the buyer's experience to fill your calendar and avoid the demo/upsell fear.
cards.use_when: Recruiting and conducting customer interviews to extract buyer insights for personas, messaging or product decisions.

cards.title: Incentivize hard-to-reach interview participants
cards.summary: Match the incentive to the participant's status: product perks for normal customers, charitable donations for busy executives.
cards.use_when: Recruiting interviews with customers who are hard to book, especially senior or high-earning buyers.

cards.title: Segment personas by jobs to be done, not demographics
cards.summary: Group buyers by the job they are trying to accomplish and the trigger that makes them buy, which produces stronger segmentation than age, gender or job title.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to structure buyer personas or audience segments for campaigns, product and strategy.

cards.title: Avoid the dusty, unused persona trap
cards.summary: Most marketers create personas but never use them; build documentation that is actually referenced for campaigns, product and strategy.
cards.use_when: Auditing or replacing an existing persona doc that is not used in go-to-market work.

cards.title: Use surveys to verify interviews and capture data-centric attributes
cards.summary: Design a survey after interviews to confirm trends at scale and collect structured facts that work better in a form than in conversation.
cards.use_when: You have preliminary interview insights and want to validate them across a larger audience.

cards.title: Social listening for pain-point topics, not brand mentions
cards.summary: Track what people say about problems and frustrations rather than your brand so personas reflect real language and concerns.
cards.use_when: Adding a social listening layer to persona research or messaging development.

cards.title: Use digital intelligence to see how buyers actually behave
cards.summary: Digital intelligence tools reveal platforms, influencers and buying mindsets of the wider audience, filling in behavior that interviews cannot reliably capture.
cards.use_when: You need audience behavior, channel and buying-mindset data to complement interviews and surveys.

cards.title: Ask churned customers why they left
cards.summary: Direct outreach to churning customers reveals fixable reasons and can be acted on quickly, as in the subscription chicken-box example.
cards.use_when: Retention is slipping or cancellation rates are rising, especially when paid acquisition is getting harder.
